Hi Jane — Rishi here from Security. Thanks for the specificity — that helps. A few technical points and what I can provide quickly:

Encryption & keys
- Data at rest: AES-256; customer data keys can be managed via your KMS (we support AWS KMS/HSM brings-your-own-key in Dedicated/Private deployments).
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern cipher suites.

Access & logging
- Role-based access controls, least privilege for support engineers, 90-day credential rotation for service accounts by default.
- Audit logs: retention configurable; default 1 year for hosted, can be extended for Dedicated/Private.

FedRAMP-adjacent mapping
- We maintain a control mapping that aligns our controls to NIST SP 800-53 low/moderate where practical; we are not FedRAMP-authorized but can provide evidence for control families (AC, IA, AU, SC, SI).

DPIA inputs
- Attached is a DPIA template pre-filled with our standard processing descriptions. If you confirm data categories (PII, student education records, pseudonymized usage metrics), I will produce a short risk-treatment summary.

SCCs/DPA
- The DPA redline includes SCC language for EU transfers where applicable. For state procurement, we can offer equivalent contractual protections and data residency options in US regions.

Evidence sharing
- I can upload the SOC2 artifacts and CAIQ supporting evidence to a secure folder; please confirm the email addresses to grant access.

If you send the list of fields and retention, I will pull together the DPIA inputs and the control mapping by end of day Wed 3/4.

-Rishi

- Retention: statutory requirement is up to 7 years for certain records; procurement prefers a 7-year tier but is open to tiered deletion/archival policies.
- Evidence access: please upload SOC2 substantiation and CAIQ evidence to a secure folder and grant access to jane.park@wa-state.gov and paul.sanders@kleinprocure.com.
